Hi Aisha — thanks for the clear questions, and great timing on the renewal. Short answers up front, followed by actionable steps: 

1) Who issues the invoice
- If you buy via Azure Marketplace with Microsoft as the transacting party ("Microsoft billed"), Microsoft issues the invoice to FakeSaaS and collects payment. Redwood does not issue a customer-facing invoice in that flow; instead we provide commercial/entitlement confirmations and any necessary supplier tax info to enable your AP process.
- If the transaction is structured as "marketplace listing but vendor-billed" (Redwood invoices you directly), Redwood issues the invoice and is responsible for VAT/GST handling.

2) VAT and reverse-charge
- For EU purchases billed by Microsoft: typically Microsoft acts as the vendor of record and will include VAT treatment in the invoice (often reverse-charge for B2B in many EU countries) — your AP can self-account if Microsoft indicates reverse-charge and includes our VAT/Tax ID. We can request Microsoft to include the supplier VAT ID on the invoice; please confirm the exact billing entity they expect on your PO.
- For vendor-billed flows: we’ll need your VAT ID and company registration to zero-rate/export or apply reverse-charge depending on jurisdiction.

3) W-9 / W-8
- US legal entities: Redwood requires a completed W-9 prior to onboarding for direct-bill contracts. For marketplace billed-by-Microsoft purchases, Microsoft may still require tax forms on file for the transacting relationship.
- Non-US/foreign payees: W-8BEN-E (or equivalent local forms) if the entity is foreign and requires a US tax withholding exemption.}

Next steps I propose (we can do these in parallel):
- I attached a sample Azure co-sell invoice (azure-co-sell-invoice-sample.pdf) and our signed W-9 (redwood_w9_signed.pdf) for your AP and Microsoft submission.
- Please confirm whether your PO will list Microsoft as the billing entity or Redwood. If Microsoft, share your AP contact at Microsoft (if known) so we can coordinate supplier VAT ID inclusion.
- If Redwood will bill you directly, please send your company tax IDs (VAT/Tax ID, registered address) and the procurement checklist you mentioned; we’ll loop Finance for the final invoice template.

Ben — tagging you to confirm any Redwood finance-side requirements for vendor-bill vs marketplace-bill and whether we need an MSA addendum for marketplace transactions.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz

Hi Aisha — looping back with a final plan so you can close PO/PO date expectations. Per our discussion and coordination with Microsoft: 

1) Billing entity: Microsoft will be the transacting party on this specific quote (per the co-sell ordering flow you selected). Microsoft will issue the invoice to FakeSaaS. Redwood will not issue a duplicate customer invoice for this purchase.

2) VAT / reverse-charge: We confirmed with Microsoft that they can include Redwood's VAT/tax ID and mark the invoice for reverse-charge where applicable for B2B EU entities. Please forward this email to your AP and ask them to request Microsoft to include the supplier VAT ID on the invoice if their portal does not capture it automatically.

3) Tax forms: For completeness we've attached our signed W-9 (redwood_w9_signed.pdf). If FakeSaaS is a US legal entity and Microsoft requires a tax form for the transacting relationship, please submit the W-9 to Microsoft. For non-US subsidiaries, send the appropriate W-8/W-9 equivalent to the Microsoft AP address you use.

4) Timeline: Microsoft typically posts the marketplace invoice within 1–3 business days after payment settlement. Expect their invoice to appear in your billing portal; if it does not, escalate to azure-marketplace@microsoft.com and cc me.
